role: PlanetryItems: configurable custom items, rarity glyphs, lore, Minecraft attributes, oxygen, equipment, durability and level/skill requirements.
platform: Paper/Purpur backend plugin, not Velocity, Spigot or Folia.
compatibility: Paper/Purpur26.1.2, Java25, paper-api26.1.2.build.74-stable. No database. All participating backends must share item definitions and language files; persistent item data survives normal item serialization. Optional AuraSkills2.4.0 API, Nexo1.22+ for26.1.2, and PlanetryCore cachedProgress(UUID). Real Nexo/client/Purpur combination requires staging.
integration: Optional Nexo copies visual components and resolves tag_common/tag_uncommon/tag_rare/tag_epic/tag_legendary/tag_mythical glyphs; no source updater identity retained. Optional AuraSkills exposes five skill requirements and nonpersistent wisdom/health/regeneration/toughness/strength bonuses on active usable equipment. PlanetryCore game levels come from cachedProgress, never vanilla XP. Missing/unloaded level sources deny positive requirements. Installed disabled/incompatible NetworkInventorySync denies grants and inventory refresh until isReady(UUID). ItemService API and planetryitems:item_id/durability/oxygen PDC support future plugins. No live installation is automated. Definitions load atomically from recursive items/*.yml or .yaml; legacy root items.yml imports once to items/imported.yml. All admin commands require planetry.admin.items; /pitems info shows complete settings. Public /migrate has a durable per-backend two-hour player cooldown. Join/server-switch and reload migrations wait for Inventory Sync readiness, preserve quantities/remaining durability/foreign PDC/enchantments and remove deleted IDs with named contact-staff notices. Restricted items remain holdable in both hands without native/AuraSkills bonuses; use and armour equip stay blocked. Rarity dictates display-name color; unbreakable items have no counter/Unbreakable tooltip. Requirement denial labels exclude lore prefixes. Migration retains container/bundle contents, book text and stored enchantments. Session-bound automatic retries handle unavailable Nexo sources or insufficient split space. Stale-attribute cursor drags cancel once for safe cursor repair, then holding is allowed. Nexo native <glyph:id> tags and bitmap/colorable/shadow arguments plus <shift:N> work across item names/lore and language templates. MiniMessage target is the viewer/recipient for current native permission checks; older player-aware resolver preferred when available, global for console. Native fonts retained; rarity still owns name color. Missing/disabled/incompatible/empty/throwing glyphs use glyph-fallbacks.<id>, otherwise empty; unavailable shifts are empty. Nexo owns unknown-ID and permission behavior when active. Dynamic values stay literal and fallbacks do not recursively expand Nexo tags. Boolean canplace (default true) and soulbound (default false) accept root or bonuses entries, once each. Old planetry-canplace/planetry-soulbound remain compatible aliases; mixed spellings or repeated locations reject reload. /pitems info uses short detail labels and accepts both old/new flag placeholders in custom headers. Upgrade all backend JARs before adopting short YAML keys; persistent item keys and lore.soulbound remain unchanged. Current catalog policies apply immediately; BYTE can_place/soulbound PDC travel with managed items. Placement denial is silent; soulbound also blocks external writes/world deposits and protects nested bundle/container carriers, while own inventory/ender chest and safe retrieval remain allowed. Death retains protected stacks; full-storage restricted equipment stays worn without bonuses. /pitems soulboundbypass uses planetry.admin.items and a session-local two-second same-metadata/quantity double-drop confirmation. It never permits storage, world placement or automatic death drops. Protected cursor cleanup uses player-PDC soulbound_recovery escrow on the current backend; pending exact stacks restore when online, living and inventory-ready as space opens, retaining exact remainders without dropping leftovers. Corrupt old queues remain untouched while new cursors use independently recoverable entries. Pending recovery is not a shared Inventory Sync profile and waits on the originating backend. Protected recoverable arrows cannot fire/load; already charged protected ammunition is vetoed before crossbow mutation. Soulbound weapons with ordinary ammunition remain usable. Protected bundles refuse native content-unload use. Generic input clicks and entity interactions do not spend durability; accepted combat, mining, confirmed tool transformations/shearing, consumption, projectiles, shielding, wearing damage and flight retain completion-based custom wear. Native MAX_DAMAGE/DAMAGE mirror the custom durability ratio for breakable single items, including nonnative materials (bundles retain their native fullness bar and durability lore); the native damage/mending guards prevent duplicate vanilla wear or display-only repairs; elytra/tridents scale native capacity equally to preserve their final usable custom point. Low lore starts at 30% remaining, with the final point always included. Only ARMOUR/COSMETIC/SPACESUIT configured equipment can occupy its worn slot. Nonwearables explicitly remove EQUIPPABLE, overriding native heads/pumpkins/armour and copied Nexo components. Guarded equip routes and ready inventory reconciliation enforce current type/slot policy while both hands remain holdable; soulbound full-storage recovery retains invalid worn items without bonuses until space opens. Brushes and pig/strider control sticks use positive uncancelled native wear as their special-use completion signal (subject to native Unbreaking), spending one custom point while cancelling automatic wear; ordinary clicks remain free. Native exhausted control-stick conversion returns an ordinary fishing rod; custom metadata is cleared before native copying to prevent managed identity resurrection. Network grant API: main-thread networkItemIds(String prefix) returns immutable sorted at-most100 IDs from the current backend catalog; giveNetworkItem(UUID,String,int) returns SUCCESS/OFFLINE/UNKNOWN_ITEM/INVALID_AMOUNT/INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE/INVENTORY_FULL/UNAVAILABLE. Matching PlanetryVelocity and PlanetryVelocity-Backend route /pitems give and /planetryitems give across one proxy, requiring planetry.admin.items on Velocity. Other subcommands and backend console stay local. Grants deep-clone/stage storage, check exact current living session, catalog/readiness and unchanged inventory again before the single write, with zero partial capacity grants. Mutation exceptions propagate as uncertain; postcommit reconcile/notification failure cannot report rejected delivery. Bridge durably reserves operation IDs before mutation and never automatically retries unconfirmed delivery. Definitions/language stay backend-local; network commands do not distribute them.
validation: Java25 mvn -B -ntp clean verify dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=target/test-classpath.txt; python3 scripts/smoke.py target/planetry-items-VERSION.jar, then repeat --without-hooks. Real Paper probes use controlled players/API fixtures, not connected clients or actual Nexo/AuraSkills binaries. Stage real clients, actual optional plugins/resource pack, Purpur and cross-backend transfers. See docs/ACCEPTANCE.md. Issue11 probes include holding/bonus restrictions, info and permission gates, public migration cooldown, readiness-delayed join updates/removal, rarity colors and hidden unbreakable lore; folder/import and text regressions run in unit tests. Glyph regressions cover native argument forwarding, fonts, current/global and older player-aware resolver APIs, missing/disabled/incompatible/failing hooks and safe fallbacks. Packaged Paper probes exercise configured names/lore/messages, viewer forwarding and serialized glyph components with controlled Nexo API fixtures in both integration modes. Context-target and recipient permission isolation regressions model current native APIs; original simple-glyph ItemLanguage API remains compatible. Policy parser/language tests cover boolean defaults, invalid/duplicate fields and retained-language fallback. Paper probes cover old/current/saved flags and serialization, silent both-hand placement, click/shift/hotbar/offhand/drag/bundle routes, actual ender-inventory identity, nested carriers, creative and held-drop confirmations, metadata/quantity/timeout/session/permission fences, death retention and full-storage equipment. Cursor escrow probes exercise close/quit/death, exact byte round trips, capacity/readiness gating, service restart, repeated/partial recovery beyond storage capacity, bundle unload vetoes and corrupt-data retention with independently saved new cursors. Controlled fixtures do not prove connected-client packet behavior, actual protection-plugin ordering or network player-data portability. Ammunition probes cover refused bow shots/crossbow loads, intact preloaded protected projectiles and ordinary-ammo positive controls. Short/legacy policy aliases have strict parser tests, equivalence/duplicate checks and packaged Paper reload-retention/info-placeholder probes. Documentation snippets load through the production parser, and the complete 35-attribute table is checked against the pinned Paper API constants. Issue18 regression probes cover unchanged counters on air/block/entity clicks in both hands, accepted/cancelled completion events including tool transformations, shearing, ignition and fishing, actual native bar visibility/width and component ratio on creation/use/refresh/migration/serialization, single/huge maxima and mending guards and the earlier red threshold. Equipment controls cover nonwearable native heads/pumpkins/armour, stale components, configured wearable slots, click/shift/hotbar/offhand/drag/swap/dispenser paths and restored inventories. Connected-client rendering and arbitrary external-plugin ordering remain staging checks. Special-tool probes cover input clicks, positive/cancelled/zero native wear and both hands. Actual native empty-stack conversion regressions verify both exhausted control-stick types in each hand produce ordinary rods without retained custom metadata. Issue19 adds ItemGrants unit regressions and networkGrants real-Paper probes for current reflection API, bounded/live catalogs, offthread/disabled/missing sessions, readiness/session/catalog/inventory changes before commit, stack splitting and full-inventory atomicity, deep-copy metadata preservation, uncertain writes and postcommit notification/reconciliation failures. Run matched backend bridge smoke with --items-jar actual Items JAR for actual reflected APIs/ItemStacks; controlled sessions do not establish real-client cross-backend transport.
